name: Fluffy Buttermilk-Style Pancakes (Small Batch)
ingredients:
1 cup whole milk
2 tsp lemon juice
1 cup all-purpose flour
1/3 cup almond flour
1 1/2 tbsp cane sugar
1 1/4 tsp baking powder
1/4 tsp baking soda
1/4 tsp salt
1 large egg
2 tbsp melted butter, plus more for the pan
3/4 tsp vanilla
3/4 cup maple syrup, for serving
directions:
1. Stir 2 tsp lemon juice into 1 cup whole milk and let it sit until slightly thickened and curdled-looking.
2. In a large bowl, whisk together 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1/3 cup almond flour, 1 1/2 tbsp cane sugar, 1 1/4 tsp baking powder, 1/4 tsp baking soda, and 1/4 tsp salt.
3. Whisk 1 large egg, 2 tbsp melted butter, and 3/4 tsp vanilla into the soured milk until smooth.
4. Pour wet into dry and fold just until no dry streaks remain — lumps are good, overmixing makes tough pancakes. Rest the batter while the pan heats.
5. Heat a skillet or griddle over medium heat, film with butter, and pour ~1/3 cup per pancake. Cook until bubbles form and edges look set, about 2-3 minutes, then flip and cook 1-2 minutes more.
6. Serve hot with butter and maple syrup.
description: Scaled-down batch — about 8 pancakes for 2 adults and a toddler
notes: Lumpy batter = fluffy pancakes, so stop folding early. First pancake is the pan-temperature test. Silver-dollar size for Scarlett cooks about a minute faster per side. Keep finished ones warm in a 200°F oven.
